geometry_edits.rationale: Slightly strengthen the stepped upper reduction while preserving the dominant bar.
Reduce the bend a bit to keep the mass more continuous and less kinked in section.
Wrap the existing dominant solid with a courtyard-type public void so the access edge can read as a real threshold.
Keep the courtyard modest and attached to the inherited mass rather than turning the project into a hollow ring.
Open the courtyard toward the verified access side.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the carved void with the verified access side in the program frame so the street edge becomes legible.
Broaden the access cut to read as a public threshold rather than a token notch.
Increase the depth of the carve so it produces usable ground-space consequence.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass: a bent-and-set back bar with a clear stepped silhouette, visible in all views without obvious inter-view collisions. It fits the neighborhood living brief reasonably well as a compact capacity-aware mass, and the step logic is not arbitrary because it preserves a dominant bar while reducing upper bulk. The main weakness is the public threshold: the blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly, with no strong court, undercut, notch, or entry seam that would make the ground edge legible. The form is therefore program-fit enough to pass, but it needs a stronger carved void or access-oriented ground response to fully satisfy the semantic contract.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More courtyard/pavilion-like than the candidate; its stronger public threshold and enclosure logic are not yet present here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced massing can support a compact public program when the ground edge stays porous and the upper bulk reads as one family of stacked occupiable plates.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate is more object-like and less spatially open; the reference depends on garden enclosure rather than this form's current court-making.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A restrained perimeter mass can work if it frames a meaningful outdoor room and uses openings to activate the ground plane.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Mostly interior and facade cues; limited direct massing instruction beyond ground activation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Active low edge and clear interior-to-exterior threshold are more important than formal complexity for neighborhood commercial use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower typology is only partially transferable; avoid reading it as permission for generic vertical stacking.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked/stepped upper mass can be legible when anchored by a calmer base and a clear public ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual typology; useful only for void-making and passage, not overall building form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A bridge-like or lifted condition can intensify pedestrian/public passage when the void is the main event.

warnings: The verified access edge is not strongly activated; the ground response feels semantically neutral rather than public.
Void/publicness is the weakest concept: the subtraction reads small and secondary compared with the stepped mass.
If this were to be refined, the next move should preserve the dominant stepped bar and carve a clearer entry court or notch on the access side.
